title: incident-bot: enhance slo-toolkit on-call helpers and compact runbook links
author: Priya Kapoor
description:
Summary: Improve on-call helper utilities in the slo-toolkit and incident-bot integration. This PR adds compact runbook link generation, context-aware SLO hints, and a small helper library for adding prioritized quicklinks to on-call messages.

Motivation: On recent incidents we observed noisy runbook links and low signal in automated suggestions. This makes it faster for on-call engineers to find the most relevant remediation steps and reduces cognitive load when paging.

Related Linear: ENG-3421, SRE-78.

Checklist:
- [x] Add compact runbook link formatter (incident-bot)
- [x] Expose prioritized quicklinks helper in slo-toolkit
- [x] Add context-aware SLO hint generation (heuristics + sampling)
- [x] Unit tests for new helpers
- [x] End-to-end smoke test with incident-bot message render
- [x] Docs + examples updated

What changed (high level):
- incident-bot: new compactRunbookFormatter that produces short, on-call-friendly links with priority badges and optional SLO snippets
- slo-toolkit: new oncall/helpers/prioritizedQuicklinks and oncall/helpers/sloHints modules
- infra: updated message rendering pipeline to include prioritized quicklinks when available
- docs: updated runbook linking guide and added example usage in on-call playbooks

Commits (summary):
- 1f2a3b4: add compact runbook formatter and initial unit tests
- 2c3d4e5: expose prioritized quicklinks helper in slo-toolkit API
- 3d4e5f6: wire prioritized quicklinks into incident-bot message renderer
- 4e5f6a7: add heuristics for context-aware SLO hints and sampling fallback
- 5f6a7b8: docs + examples + changelog

Updates to files (high level):
- incident-bot/src/render/compact_runbook_formatter.py (new)
- slo-toolkit/src/oncall/helpers/prioritized_quicklinks.py (new)
- slo-toolkit/src/oncall/helpers/slo_hints.py (new)
- incident-bot/src/render/message_pipeline.py (modified)
- docs/oncall/runbook-linking.md (modified)
- tests/* (added unit + integration smoke tests)

Small illustrative snippet (rendering logic): "priority_label = 'P0' if score > 0.9 else 'P1'"

Review summary (thread highlights):
- Ethan Miller (reviewer): "Nice work — compact links look much cleaner. Two nits: 1) prefer explicit import paths in the toolkit exports, 2) add a test for the sampling fallback when SLO metadata is missing."
- Author (Priya): "Thanks — addressed both nits in a follow-up commit and added regression tests."
- Sara Liu (approver): "Approvals from SRE and runtime owners. Verified smoke test locally; message render looks good in Slack staging."
- Diego Ramos (comment): "Consider exposing a configurable threshold for priority tiers (0.8 vs 0.9). Not required for this PR but added to roadmap notes."

CI status: initial CI run had one flaky integration test (tests/integration/test_message_render.py::test_compact_links) fail on first run (timeout on Slack API stub). Re-ran CI; all checks passed on second run.

CI checks:
- unit: pass
- integration: pass
- lint: pass
- mypy: pass
- deploy-preview: pass

Files changed count: 6; additions: 412; deletions: 120

Backwards compatibility / breaking changes: none. This is additive and guarded by feature flags in incident-bot config.

Release notes: "Enhancement: incident-bot now surfaces compact runbook links and prioritized quicklinks in on-call messages (slo-toolkit helpers). This improves signal for on-call engineers and reduces noise in paging messages. To opt-in, enable `prioritized_quicklinks` in incident-bot config. See docs/oncall/runbook-linking.md for details."

Testing and rollout plan:
- Feature flagged behind incident-bot config flag `prioritized_quicklinks` (default off)
- Rollout to staging, monitor oncall-message latency and oncall-reaction feedback
- Gradually enable for 10% then 100% of incidents for staging followed by prod after 48h with no regressions

Observability: Added metrics: incident_bot.runbook.links.render_time_ms and slo_toolkit.oncall.quicklinks.generated_count; added tracing hook in message_pipeline.render() for sampling analysis

Security implications: none (links are to internal runbook IDs; we continue to avoid leaking customer identifiers)

Merge method: squash and merge. Merged-by: Sara Liu (squash).
